title: Data controls intake: weighted funnel and action bundles
creator: Priya Nair
description: Goal: Build a deterministic intake funnel for customer data-control requests (logging redaction, retention changes, PII handling, audit exports) that produces a weighted priority score and a small set of prescriptive action bundles. The intake should reduce manual routing time, ensure regulatory-sensitive requests get legal/KMS review, and produce clear SLAs for response and delivery. Deliverables: 1) intake form schema and automated router, 2) weighted scoring rubric, 3) three action bundles (Config Change, Engineered Fix, Escalation to Legal/Support), 4) documentation and runbook for SRE/Support to act on requests.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form implemented in Zendesk/Forms with fields needed for scoring (customer tier, data type, retention delta, PII presence, regulator jurisdiction)
Automated routing in our intake lambda assigns requests to the correct queue (Support / Security / Legal / Eng) >= 95% on sample dataset
Decision rubric defined and published (score components + thresholds) and reviewed by Legal and Security
Three action bundles documented with required artifacts and estimated lead times (Config Change <= 5 business days, Engineered Fix 2-8 weeks, Escalation variable)
Runbook created and linked in support playbooks with example ticket flows and fallback when dependencies block work
proposed_routing_rules: Score >= 80 -> High-priority legal+security review; SLA: initial ack < 4 hours
Score 50-79 -> Product/Support resolve with optional engineering task; SLA: initial ack < 24 hours
Score < 50 -> Triage queue; target response < 3 business days; suggest templated customer guidance
decision_rubric: Customer tier weight: Enterprise=30, Mid-market=15, Self-serve=5
Data sensitivity: PII/Sensitive=30, Internal logs=10, Metrics-only=5
Engineering effort estimate (points): 0-2 -> subtract 5, 3-8 -> 0, >8 -> add 10 (to surface high-effort/high-impact)
Business impact override: CS/AE can flag 'customer-critical' to add 20 points with audit log justification
action_bundles: Config Change Bundle: For retention or redaction changes that are purely config-driven (e.g., retention TTL changes, log sampling adjustments). Includes required customer form, config PR template, and rollback plan. Target MTTD: 5 business days.

Engineered Fix Bundle: For requests that require code/runtime changes (KV-cache pruning, structured redaction pipelines, export format changes). Includes tech spec template, impact scope, test plan, and rollout checklist. Target delivery: 2-8 weeks depending on estimate.

Escalation + Legal Bundle: For PII exports, regulator-driven retention overrides, or requests requiring contractual changes. Includes pre-submission legal questionnaire, KMS/access review checklist, and audit export format spec. SLA: initial legal intake < 48 hours, timeline dependent on contract/legal review.
comments: 2025-02-20 Priya Nair: Draft rubric shared with Legal and Security for feedback. Emphasized need for customer-tier weighting to avoid over-indexing on low-value self-serve tickets.

2025-02-24 Diego Martinez: Engineering flagged runtime redaction complexity — some redaction asks will require model-level inference changes and KV-cache considerations. Proposed gating such asks into Engineered Fix Bundle only after feasibility spike.

2025-02-28 Alyssa Chen (Design): Prototyped intake form with progressive disclosure (show only fields relevant after selecting request type). This reduces noisy attributes and improves completion rate.

2025-03-03 Legal (Marcus Lee): Approved rubric base weights but requested an explicit field for 'contractual data obligations' and that any override be auditable in the ticket history. Asked for sample legal questionnaire added to bundle.

2025-03-05 Support (Maya Patel): Suggested we add templated customer responses for common low-score requests to reduce manual response time. Also proposed a 'self-service KB flow' when request is config-supported.

2025-03-06 Diego Martinez: Added dependency on PM-71211 (intake lambda auth work) and PM-33124 (triage taxonomies). Marking security_review_required=true per Legal feedback. Next: engineering spike to estimate typical Engineered Fixs (2w).
risks_and_tradeoffs: Automating routing reduces manual triage but risks misclassification — mitigated by human-in-loop fallback for first 30 days and weekly sampling audits.
Weighting customer tier increases speed for high-revenue accounts but may deprioritize smaller customers; include CS escalation path to override scores with justification.
Exposing retention changes as self-serve config reduces support load but increases chance of misconfiguration; require validation checks and safe rollback window.
Engineering can reduce time with templated PRs and small-scope patches; larger structural redactions may require model/infra coordination and cross-team planning.
next_steps: 1) Finalize intake form fields and implement prototype in Zendesk by 2025-03-14
2) Kick engineering spike (2 weeks) to validate feasibility and cost of common Engineered Fix scenarios
3) Legal to provide the questionnaire and approval language by 2025-03-10
4) Build router rules and a simple score calculator service (internal) to produce routing decisions and audit trail
5) Pilot with 3 enterprise customers for 4 weeks and collect false-positive/negative rates
